profile.summary: I am a graduate software engineer focused on building full-stack applications, backend systems, data-driven tools, and AI-enabled software. My experience includes professional software development and IT support, production deployment, cloud infrastructure, database design, technical collaboration, and product development. I co-founded and engineered FuelLinkPro, an on-demand fuel delivery platform, and have worked on applications addressing problems in education, document verification, event management, and skills intelligence. My current work at Wits involves software development within the Future of Learning environment, including systems connected to skills mapping, research workflows, and emerging technologies. I am interested in engineering reliable software, applying AI responsibly, and developing technology that solves practical problems.

projects.name: FuelLinkPro
projects.problem: Drivers stranded with empty fuel tanks, rural machinery operators, and commercial fleet managers face significant downtime when vehicles run out of fuel far from commercial filling stations. Traditional roadside assistance is slow and lacks real-time dispatch transparency.
projects.solution: A three-sided on-demand marketplace connecting consumers with mobile fuel delivery providers. Customers place geotagged orders with vehicle and fuel specifications; certified drivers receive dispatch requests, navigate via Google Maps, and complete verified deliveries; administrators monitor safety compliance, payments, and platform commission splits.
projects.my_contribution: Sole-engineered the entire backend architecture: PostgreSQL database modeling, Flask RESTful API services, JWT session validation, PayFast payment gateway integration with cryptographic hash verification, Celery background worker queues for automated timeout handling, Socket.IO live order dispatch events, and production Docker/Nginx deployment.
projects.architecture: Client web & mobile interface communicating with a Gunicorn-managed Flask API. Persistence handled by PostgreSQL with SQLAlchemy ORM. Redis provides in-memory state caching and serves as Celery broker for background notifications. Nginx operates as a reverse proxy terminating SSL.
projects.reported_traction: Over 10 registered customers and over 15 onboarded drivers prepared for fulfillment. Note: These are supplied project figures reflecting early rollout onboarding, not verified active daily usage or audited revenue metrics.
projects.business_model_note: Operates an on-demand driver split model. An initial prototype considered an 80/20 driver commission; the current operating model evaluates a 70/30 split to balance platform operational and insurance overhead.

projects.name: Wits Skills Mapping Platform
projects.problem: Traditional career exploration tools rely on static occupational taxonomies that fail to reflect evolving technical skills and real industry requirements, leaving students and workforce development researchers with disconnected data.
projects.solution: An intelligent platform that extracts and maps candidate skills from curriculum vitae, visualizes transferable competencies, and matches candidate profiles against evolving industry occupations using structured ontologies and cognitive assessment telemetry.
projects.my_contribution: Designed backend API services in FastAPI and Next.js, built database schemas for storing skills taxonomies and candidate interaction telemetry in Supabase/PostgreSQL, and helped design safe integration boundaries for AI-assisted competency extraction.
projects.architecture: Next.js frontend communicating with a FastAPI microservice layer. Relational data and session state managed through Supabase and PostgreSQL. Strict privacy controls isolate student telemetry from public endpoints.
projects.institutional_safeguards: Public documentation excludes internal server configurations, private institutional endpoints, unpublished research datasets, and private API credentials.

projects.name: Darkroom DataForge
projects.tagline: Structured Data Extraction, Validation, and Dataset Generation
projects.problem: Complex unstructured documents such as institutional reports, scans, and multi-page technical manuals contain critical tabular records that break standard optical character recognition tools, leading to corrupted numbers, lost page boundaries, and unverified data.
projects.solution: An auditable data extraction pipeline based on the core engineering principle: 'Every extracted record should be traceable to its source.' Follows a pipeline of Ingestion -> Classification -> Extraction -> Table Reconstruction -> Normalization -> Validation -> Human-in-the-Loop Review -> Export.
projects.my_contribution: Engineered document parsing services, designed tabular reconstruction heuristics to handle multi-page table splits, implemented record-level bounding box coordinate provenance, and built export pipelines for CSV, JSON, and Excel formats.
projects.architecture: React & TypeScript frontend interface paired with a high-throughput FastAPI backend. Database layer built with SQLAlchemy supporting PostgreSQL in containerized production and SQLite in local developer sandboxes.
projects.key_principle: Traceability and human review help researchers inspect the exact document page and coordinate evidence behind structured records before committing them to research datasets.

projects.name: VerifySA
projects.problem: Small businesses and institutions struggle with fraudulent certificates, doctored invoices, and falsified national documents, but enterprise identity verification tools are prohibitively expensive and slow to integrate.
projects.solution: A rapid-verification SaaS prototype combining multimodal LLM document extraction with deterministic business-rule validation, generating transparent trust scores and verifiable PDF audit reports.
projects.my_contribution: Led a 10-person developer team during an intensive 5-hour hackathon sprint at the Soweto AI App Development Challenge. Architected the Next.js 15 application structure, coordinated backend schema design on Supabase, and implemented the hybrid rule validation pipeline.
projects.architecture: Next.js 15 with React 19 and TypeScript on Vercel edge infrastructure. Supabase provides PostgreSQL storage and authentication. OpenAI GPT-4o extracts structured data from uploaded documents, which is immediately piped through deterministic validation functions.
projects.honest_disclosure: VerifySA was built as a rapid 5-hour hackathon sprint proof-of-concept. It combines heuristic rule checks with LLM analysis; AI extraction alone does not constitute legal proof of authenticity, and no verified production fraud detection rates are claimed without formal benchmark datasets.

projects.name: merSETA Layer 0 Ingestion & Reconciliation Engine
projects.tagline: Fail-Closed Document Ingestion & Mathematical Reconciliation Engine
projects.role: Backend Software Engineer / Data Platform Engineer
projects.problem: Unstructured South African skills demand and labor market documents (Sector Skills Plans, TVET reports, WSP/ATR filings) contain subtle OCR and text extraction errors (misaligned numbers, shifted columns). Ingesting corrupted figures causes national policy forecasting to rely on invalid data, violating South African Auditor-General (AGSA) compliance standards.
projects.solution: Built a mission-critical, fail-closed data ingestion pipeline that ingests, extracts, cleans, mathematically audits, and vaults unstructured documents before publishing them to downstream analytics models. Implements a 10-step lifecycle with exact Python Decimal arithmetic (zero IEEE 754 float drift) and two-phase durable dispatch.
projects.my_contribution: Architected the complete 10-step ingestion lifecycle: dropzone watcher with stability heuristics, SHA-256 pre-hashing, vector vs raster PDF triage with PyMuPDF drawing trees, precision table extraction via pdfplumber, Pydantic v2 schema validation, exact Decimal mathematical reconciliation bridge, fail-closed publication gates, and durable two-phase downstream dispatch.
projects.architecture: Python 3.12 managed with uv, PyMuPDF for vector layout triage, pdfplumber for coordinate-bounded table extraction, Pydantic v2 domain schemas, Supabase content-addressed vault storage (raw-unstructured/{YYYY}/{sha256}.{ext}), and HTTP dispatch to downstream Rust analytics orchestrators.
projects.quality_gates: 332 hermetic unit tests executing in under 25 seconds with 100% mathematical reconciliation parity across all parsed tables. Zero IEEE 754 floating-point drift.

projects.architecture: TanStack Start full-stack SSR application on React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, custom LOAM design system, and grounded backend retrieval pipeline with bounding-box coordinate tracking.

engineering_principles.principle: Understand the problem before selecting a solution
engineering_principles.description: Software complexity is costly. I spend time clarifying user workflows, domain constraints, and data requirements before choosing libraries, frameworks, or cloud infrastructure.

engineering_principles.principle: Design reliable backend services and defensive data models
engineering_principles.description: Databases are the bedrock of any serious system. I enforce relational integrity, strict constraints, secure authorization, and idempotent handlers at the database and API boundary.

engineering_principles.principle: Build interfaces around real user workflows
engineering_principles.description: Whether an on-demand fuel order, a document audit interface, or a campus event checkout, every UI component exists to help a human accomplish their task without confusion or friction.

engineering_principles.principle: Integrate external services and AI responsibly
engineering_principles.description: External APIs and LLMs are powerful but prone to network latency, failure, or hallucination. I isolate third-party calls behind fallback boundaries, deterministic validation, and strict error handling.

engineering_principles.principle: Document technical decisions and acknowledge limitations
engineering_principles.description: Engineering excellence requires intellectual honesty. I clearly document architectural trade-offs, security considerations, and known boundaries rather than making unsupported claims.
